vo: Here is the laziest way I know to turn Grok Bot into money. No big team, no complicated stack. Just one small idea, and a crew of Bots that does the heavy lifting.

Being lazy is fine. Lazy people look for the shortest path, and today the shortest path is selling a service that Bots deliver for you. There are thousands of ways to do it. This is the one I would pick if I had to start from zero, and wanted money fast, with the least effort.
Step one. Build a simple landing page with a no-code page builder. One page, one clear promise. It is the shop window for your new little agency, and it takes an afternoon, not a month.
Next, pick a niche. Gym owners. Restaurants. Gardeners. Window cleaners. Plumbers. The list never ends, so do not agonize over it.
Choose one you already know. Maybe your dad runs a landscaping company. Then you already understand how the day goes, what annoys people, and what they would happily pay to make go away.

Now the real work: think inside their business. Picture the landscaper. He is cutting grass all day. Does he have time to reply to Google reviews? No. He answers the phone, but only after he turns the mower off. Does he even have a website? And where do his customers come from?
Maybe he has no portfolio either. All those perfect lawn stripes, and nobody can see them. Every one of those little gaps is a product you could sell.

Run the same check on a plumber. Does he have a Google profile? A website? Is he running ads, or does he only get work by word of mouth? Ten minutes of honest questions will show you where the pain is.
Put it in a table with three columns. One: the niche. Two: their pain point. Three: how you can help, with something they will actually appreciate, and something you can charge for.

Here is the trap. Not every business needs every agent. Take a plumber friend of mine. He does not care whether anyone replies to his reviews. He does not even ask customers to leave one. A reply bot would be wasted on him.
But he is self-employed, so invoices and accounts keep him up at night. That is the real need. Sell the thing they actually need, not the thing you are excited to build.

And sell it monthly. A service business that likes your agent will pay every month, and that recurring income is what makes this worth the effort. The one-off sale is nice. The subscription is the point.
So you have a niche, a pain point, and an offer. Next question: how do you actually get customers? That is where the lazy part comes in.
